Ceviche is a traditional Latin American dish of raw seafood marinated in citrus juice, most famously associated with Peru where it is the national dish and recognized by UNESCO. The dish is prepared by denaturing fish proteins with citric acid, which firms the flesh without using heat. Its origins trace back to pre-Hispanic coastal civilizations in South America, which used local acids like banana passionfruit or fermented corn beer before the arrival of European citrus. The modern dish is a fusion that emerged in the colonial period and is typically served with starchy sides to balance its acidity.
